body:
P4-24 BUILT (code PR), not walked. How it hangs together: ONE stored setting (AppSettings.dataSaver, Settings > Playback, one line under the two quality rows, hidden where the platform cannot report mobile data) and ONE derived value, dataSaverInForceProvider (app/providers.dart) = switch on AND NetworkKind.mobile (Ethernet, offline and VPN over Wi-Fi are not mobile; networkKindOf is pure and tested). The four consumers read only that value: (1) streaming quality = streamQualityProvider (choice for the link, held to AudioQuality.cappedForDataSaver()); (2) new downloads = DownloadPolicy.dataSaver, capped in DownloadManager._startOne, made-at recorded in Downloads.quality; (3) pictures = CoverBudget.mobile for every cover widget (CoverArtResolver) and the lock-screen art; the background prefetch uses the SAME CoverBudget (its old 'mobile: small only, 120' rule now lives there, no copy); (4) prepare-ahead = prepareAheadSongs() = 1 instead of 2 (the engine asks each tick, so a change of link applies at once). The cap never changes the codec: Original -> Opus 48, Opus 160/96 -> Opus 48, Compatible (MP3, no lower MP3 level exists) stays and the switch's line says so.

Downloads (ruling 1, built in this PR): schema v8 adds Downloads.refresh_quality (nullable: the quality a queued/running REFRESH is asked at; `quality` keeps naming the copy on the phone). The planner upgrades a copy only when it is exactly what the cap makes of the wanted quality (upgradeCapped, Wi-Fi and cap not in force), with the failed-download back-off; the transfer requires Wi-Fi whatever 'Wi-Fi only' says; a queued upgrade is held off Wi-Fi and does not block first downloads; the new file replaces the old one only when complete (existing .new swap). FOUND AND FIXED on the way: a TRANSFER failure of any refresh used to mark the row failed and the retry then dropped the old copy's path; it now leaves the old copy playable (restoreDone) and deletes the partial file.

Left for later, on purpose: a metered Wi-Fi hotspot (ruling 3); NetworkKind merges Wi-Fi and Ethernet, so the grey note says 'not on mobile data', not 'on Wi-Fi'; when the switch flips while a song plays, the already-loaded next source keeps the quality it was resolved at (the following ones follow); a large cover already cached is not reused when the small one is missing (one small fetch). Syncing less on mobile data is P1-14's (note handed over). Byte-count acceptance (the phone's per-app data counter on mobile data) is for a real walk on the release-candidate pair.
